summary: Embeddings shard compaction loop triggering proxy backoff and elevated 5xx
description:
Issue summary:
A sustained elevation of 5xx responses was observed for a dedicated tenant after a background embeddings shard compaction job entered a tight retry/scan loop. The compaction loop caused high KV-store IO and long shard-level lock hold times, which escalated upstream timeouts and triggered API gateway backoff and proxy retries.

Impact:
- ~12% 5xx error rate for LexaSearch traffic in us-west between 2026-03-13 02:45 and 2026-03-13 05:10 UTC.
- Customer reported degraded throughput for bulk embedding uploads and increased end-to-end latencies for embedder-v2.1 requests.
- Streaming sessions experienced intermittent resets when requests fanout to the affected shard.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-west) serving dedicated tenant LexaSearch.
- Affected model: embedder-v2.1 pinned by tenant.
- Background maintenance: automated shard compaction scheduled daily at 02:30 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Tenant triggers large bulk embeddings upload (~1.6M vectors) + concurrent small batch inference traffic.
2) Scheduled shard compaction starts and attempts to reconcile tombstones across multiple KV segments.
3) Compaction loop repeatedly acquires shard compaction lock and performs heavy reads/rewrites leading to IO stall and elevated KV latency.
4) API gateway sees upstream latency increases, amplifies retry/backoff behavior and begins returning 502/503/504s to clients.

Observed behavior:
- High p95/p99 latencies on kv.put/kv.scan with visible lock hold times in shard manager logs.
- API gateway logs show elevated 502 and 504 codes with upstream response timeouts.
- Runtime logs show repeated compaction job start/abort cycles for shard id=4512.
- Disk IO (nvme) throughput spike during compaction window.

Expected behavior:
- Compaction should back off gracefully when KV latencies or IO thresholds are exceeded and should not hold shard-level locks for >30s.

Relevant logs/links:
- Grafana dashboards: /d/ops/kv-store-latency?orgId=1&from=2026-03-13T02:00:00Z&to=2026-03-13T06:00:00Z
- API gateway error summary: /d/ops/apigw-errors?tenant=lexasearch&from=2026-03-13T02:30Z
- Runtime compaction trace: s3://redwood-logs/prod/kv/compaction/2026-03-13/shard-4512.log
comments: 2026-03-13 03:10 - Support (Aisha): Created ticket after customer reported increased 5xx rate (~12%) and slow embedding uploads. Initial triage: suspect compaction coincident with bulk upload.

2026-03-13 03:40 - SRE (Marco): Correlated compaction schedule start (02:31 UTC) with KV latency spike. Observed repeated compaction start/abort entries for shard-4512. Rolling disable of compaction for shard-4512 requested.

2026-03-13 04:05 - Customer (LexaSearch - Jamie): Confirmed errors subsided around 04:12 UTC after you said you disabled background compaction. Thanks — upload throughput resumed but some earlier vectors are missing consistency markers.

2026-03-13 07:20 - Eng (Priya): Reproduced locally. Hypothesis: tombstone reconciliation bug in compaction loop causes IO re-writes and fails to honor backoff when encountering concurrent writes. Preparing patch and test harness.

2026-03-14 01:05 - SRE (Marco): Hotfix applied to disable aggressive compaction and to add rate limiting on compaction retries. Monitoring shows 5xx rate has returned to baseline (<0.5%) for LexaSearch since 2026-03-13 04:15 UTC.
2026-03-14 09:30 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. Opened follow-up task for clean resync of affected shard and consistency verification.

2026-03-14 11:00 - Eng (Priya): PR merged (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3821) that adds compaction backoff and lock-time safeguards. Will roll canary to us-west tonight (2026-03-14 22:00 UTC).
investigation_notes: Observed compaction job churn: job start -> partial scan -> abort -> immediate retry (no exponential backoff).
Shard-level lock hold times peaked at ~85s during the incident (expected <30s).
nvme_io throughput increased by 6x compared to baseline during compaction window. IO wait correlated with kv.put latency increase.
Disabling compaction for shard-4512 reduced 5xx rate from 12% -> 0.4% within 10 minutes. This verifies compaction loop as primary driver.
Hypothesis: tombstone reconciliation loop triggers full-segment rewrite in presence of concurrent small writes; a bug causes immediate retry without respecting global IO throttles.
Temporary mitigation options evaluated: pause compaction, limit compaction concurrency, or increase compaction backoff. Chose pause + patch to add backoff.
Ran a canary test with synthetic embed upload and compaction; confirmed compaction backoff prevents lock storms and keeps apigw error rate <1%.
Investigated connected subsystems: scheduler (respects compaction flags), api-gateway (observed increased retries), serving-runtime (observed transient OOMs for workers under IO pressure).
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 04:08 UTC): paused background compaction on shard-4512 and applied temporary rate limit to compaction scheduler. Hotfix merged to add exponential backoff and max lock-hold time check. Permanent fix (PR #3821) merged 2026-03-14; scheduled canary rollout 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC and full rollout 2026-03-15 03:00 UTC after verification.

Workarounds for customer: resume uploads in staggered windows, avoid running large bulk uploads during maintenance window until rollout completes. We will perform consistency verification and, if needed, run a controlled shard resync during low-traffic hours (2026-03-15 05:00 UTC).

Follow-ups: create automated guardrails in compaction scheduler to detect high KV latencies and auto-pause; add alert that maps compaction lock hold >45s -> high priority paging; postmortem to be written by Eng/SRE and shared with customer.
